newsitem.title: UK: Sports bodies back Wembley for UK national stadium.
newsitem.headline: Sports bodies back Wembley for UK national stadium.

text.p: Wembley became favourite to be named as home for Britain's new national stadium after its bid was backed by soccer, athletics and rugby league on Monday.
The governing bodies of all three sports said they would rather the proposed all-purpose stadium were built on the north London site than in Manchester -- the only other option.

While the opinions of the governing bodies are not binding, their views have left Manchester's bid in tatters. A final decision by the British government's Sports Council is expected before the end of the year. Wembley Stadium is a wholly owned subsidiary of Wembley Plc.

"The F.A. and the Football League, as event holders, and in consultation with the Premier League, have chosen Wembley as their preferred venue for the national stadium," said F.A. chief executive Graham Kelly.

British Athletic Federation executive chairman Peter Radford said: "It is our ambition to stage major world and European events and our international colleagues tell us London -- and in particular Wembley with its rich sporting history -- would have an outstanding chance in any bidding process.
"We've been playing continuously at Wembley since 1929 and there is so much illustrious history attached to Wembley in rugby league terms," said Rugby Football League chief executive Maurice Lindsay.
